title: Candida albicans Biofilm Chip (CaBChip) for High-throughput Antifungal Drug Screening
protocol: Place the microscope slides in a removable slide rack.
Wash the slides twice by immersing them in 99% ethanol (histological grade).
Dry the slides using a jet of compressed nitrogen gas after wiping with paper towels.
Immerse the slide rack containing the slides in concentrated sulphuric acid and incubate at room temperature overnight.
Sonicate the slides for 30 min.
Wash the slides with Milli-Q water for 30 min, followed by another wash in acetone for 5 min.
Coat the clean slides with a 2.5% (vol/vol in water) solution of 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES).
Wash the coated slides three times in Milli-Q water for 15 min each wash.
Bake the slides in a furnace at 110 °C for 15 min.
Using a spin coater, add 2.0 mL of PS-MA onto a clean glass slide.
Coat the slide at 3,000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Store coated slides in a slide rack under dry, dust-free conditions at 2-8°C for up to one month.
Inoculate a single colony of C. albicans SC5314 into 10 - 20 mL of YPD liquid medium.
Incubate the culture in an orbital shaker at 150 - 200 rpm and 30 °C overnight.
Centrifuge 1 mL of Candida albicans yeast cells from overnight cultures at 5,000 rpm for 5-10 minutes to harvest cells.
Wash harvested cells twice with 1 mL sterile phosphate buffered saline (PBS) per wash.
Centrifuge washed cells at 1900 rpm for 10 minutes to harvest.
Resuspend washed cells in 1 mL reconstruction buffer.
Count cells using a hemocytometer on a bright field microscope.
Adjust cell density to 5×10^7 cells/mL.
Further dilute the suspension ten times with 10× RPMI-1640 supplemented with L-glutamine and buffered with morpholinepropanesulfonic acid (MOPS).
Mix the cell suspension in RPMI-1640 with collagen to achieve a final concentration of 4× 10^6 cells/mL.
Clean all surfaces of the microarrayer with 70% isopropanol.
Place and hold PS-MA-coated glass slides on the slide deck using vacuum.
Vortex the cell suspension in collagen vigorously.
Aspirate 100 μL of the well-mixed suspension into a well of a 96-well plate just before printing.
Place this source plate in the loading station.
Switch on the humidifier to maintain a relative humidity of 100% in the microarray chamber throughout the process.
Print 50 nL of cell suspension in an array of 48 rows and 16 columns with spots spaced 1.2 mm apart using a microarray spotter by non-contact deposition.
Prime, rinse, and vacuum-dry the tips twice after each round of printing.
Immediately after printing, place the slide in an air-tight, humidified chamber and incubate at 37 °C for 24 hr to allow biofilm formation.
Prepare working solutions of antifungal drugs from stock solutions or powder in RPMI-1640 medium.
Dilute the antifungal working solution by two-fold increments to prepare eight different concentrations spanning a range with estimated IC50.
Print 50 nL of each drug concentration, positive control (no drug), and negative control on biofilms using microarrayer.
Incubate CaBChip in humidified chamber at 37 °C for 24 hr after adding drugs.
Wash CaBChip by dunking 3-5 times for 2 min in PBS to remove drugs.
Stain CaBChip with 0.5 μM FUN1 at 37 °C for 30 min.
Wash the CaBChip by dunking it 3-5 times in PBS for 1-3 min each time.
Dry the CaBChip using a nitrogen stream.
Read fluorescence intensity using a microarray scanner (GenePix 4100A, Axon Instruments, CA) at a wavelength of 532 nm with a PMT gain of 380.
Set the fluorescence intensity of the positive control (no drug) and dead (bleach-treated) biofilm spots to 100% and 0%, respectively.
Calculate percentage inhibition by reducing the fluorescence intensity relative to the average of the control spots using the given equation.
Adjust scanner settings to obtain Fmax and Fo of 30000 and 4000 RFU, respectively.
Determine the 50% inhibitory concentration (IC50) by fitting the variable slope Hill equation using GraphPad Prism Software.
